title: The Wild Hollow
premise: Zephyrine Vasquez, a bone-carver who hears the dead through the relics she carves, keeps the ledgers of the Hollow Guild, which trades in impossible things across a fragile covenant between the living world and the Hollow. When a dying courier presses a map of the covenant's broken seals into her hands, Zephyrine is branded a thief by both realms and hunted by her own guild. Guided by the voices in her bones and an exiled warden named Corvane who once enforced the law she now defies, she must reforge the covenant before the Hollow bleeds into the world at the turning of the year. In the end, Zephyrine sacrifices her gift — silencing the dead forever for her — to seal the last gate, choosing love and justice over the duty that defined her, while Corvane chooses truth over loyalty to the guild that made him.
about_author: Felix Joubert is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing funerary carvings in provincial museums before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people caught between institutions and their consciences, and live quietly near a river they refuse to name.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. We meet the Hollow Guild's counting house, where Zephyrine balances accounts of traded years, borrowed shadows, and names sold twice. A carved bone relic whispers its dead owner's grievance, unsettling her. Emotional beat: quiet competence masking loneliness; she trusts the dead more than the living.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Loading Door
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A bleeding courier collapses into the guild's loading yard at closing bell, pressing a wax-sealed map into Zephyrine's hands and dying with a warning: 'The Warden's Oath still binds.' Guild enforcers arrive too late to save him. Emotional beat: dread and reluctant responsibility as the map burns cold against her skin.

chapters.title: What the Bones Remember
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Hiding the map inside a half-carved femur, Zephyrine listens to the courier's lingering death-echo and learns his name: Ivo Merrin, once a covenant-warden. The guildmaster summons her to account for a missing ledger page. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve; she lies for the first time.

chapters.title: The Guildmaster's Smile
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Odile Vasse's POV. Odile interrogates Zephyrine gently, revealing she knows more than she says and offering protection at a price: the map, and Zephyrine's silence about what it shows. Zephyrine refuses. Emotional beat: the seduction of safety versus the first taste of defiance.

chapters.title: Flight Through the Tannery Rows
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Branded a thief, Zephyrine flees the guild quarter through smoke and dye-vats, guided by the dead voices in her satchel of carvings. She is cornered in a culvert — and saved by Corvane, an exiled warden who recognizes the map. Emotional beat: terror giving way to wary alliance.

chapters.title: The Warden Who Broke His Oath
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Corvane explains the covenant: seven seals binding the Hollow, three already broken, each breach letting something through. He was cast out for reporting the breaches; the guild buried his report. He needs Zephyrine's gift to read the map's bone-script. Emotional beat: bitter confession; two liars deciding to tell each other the truth.

chapters.title: The First Seal: Drowned Bell
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. At a flooded chapel, the pair finds the first broken seal and the thing that broke it — a drowned congregation that never finished dying. Zephyrine carves a peace from a child's rib-bone relic. Emotional beat: grief and awe; her gift becomes a burden she cannot set down.

chapters.title: Market of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. To reach the second seal, they must pass through a black market where the guild trades lifespans. Corvane sells five years of his life for passage, hiding it from Zephyrine. Emotional beat: sacrifice concealed as pragmatism; loyalty taking root without permission.

chapters.title: The Second Seal: Orchard of Teeth
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The second seal lies beneath an orchard grown from covenant-oaths; its fruit is teeth, and eating one forces you to speak only truths. Under its influence, Zephyrine admits she can hear her own dead mother among the voices. Emotional beat: intimacy through forced honesty; love beginning against both their wills.

chapters.title: Hunters in Livery
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Guild hunters led by Odile's enforcer, Sable Fen, ambush them. Corvane is recognized by his former second-in-command and offered reinstatement if he surrenders Zephyrine. He refuses and takes a wound meant to kill. Emotional beat: loyalty tested publicly; the cost of choosing becomes visible.

chapters.title: Mending What Bleeds
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Hiding in a shepherd's bothy, Zephyrine tends Corvane's wound and confesses her deepest secret: the dead don't just speak — they beg her to finish their unfinished business, and she has never once refused until now. Emotional beat: tenderness and vulnerability; duty redefined as choice rather than compulsion.

chapters.title: The Third Seal: The Empty Throne
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. The third seal sits in a ruined hall where the covenant was first sworn — and where the original signatories' ghosts still wait, bound to judge whoever comes. The ghosts demand a price: one of them must surrender their voice to the stone. Emotional beat: dread of the bargain ahead; the theme of sacrifice made explicit.

chapters.title: Odile's Bargain
chapters.summary: Odile Vasse's POV. Odile meets Zephyrine alone under a parley flag, revealing the guildmaster's true aim: not to repair the covenant but to control it, selling access between realms. She offers Zephyrine partnership and her mother's death-record as leverage. Emotional beat: temptation weaponized; Zephyrine sees her own ambition reflected back at her.

chapters.title: The Map Rewrites Itself
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The bone-map shifts, showing a fourth seal no record mentions — hidden inside the guild's own counting house, beneath the ledgers Zephyrine kept. The dead courier's echo confirms it: the rot was always at the center. Emotional beat: betrayal crystallizing into purpose; the enemy was home all along.

chapters.title: Infiltration by Ledger-Line
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Using Zephyrine's intimate knowledge of the guild's accounting codes, they infiltrate the counting house during the year-turning audit. Sable Fen catches them — but Corvane's old loyalty splits the enforcers when he reveals Odile's plan. Emotional beat: tension snapping into open schism; truth as a blade.

chapters.title: Beneath the Counting House
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Beneath the vaults they find the fourth seal — a heart of covenant-stone fed by every impossible trade the guild ever made. Breaking Odile's claim on it will collapse the guild's power. Zephyrine begins the carving that could unmake everything she served. Emotional beat: righteous fury tempered by mourning for the institution that raised her.

chapters.title: The Guildmaster Unbound
chapters.summary: Odile Vasse's POV. Cornered, Odile shatters the fourth seal deliberately, unleashing the Hollow's tide early, and offers Zephyrine a final choice: rule beside her over the ruins, or drown with everyone else. Zephyrine answers with the ledger page Odile thought destroyed — proof of Odile's first crime. Emotional beat: confrontation of mirror-selves; justice outside any law.

chapters.title: When the Hollow Comes Through
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. With four seals broken, the Hollow floods the city: memories walk, the dead queue at doors, time pools in streets. Corvane holds the counting-house steps with renegade enforcers while Zephyrine races to the original covenant site. Emotional beat: desperate heroism; ordinary people choosing to stand.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. At the empty throne, the ghost-signatories demand the price promised at the third seal: a voice surrendered to the stone. Zephyrine offers not her speaking voice but her hearing — the gift itself — carving her own fingerbone into the final seal. Emotional beat: climax; love, duty, and sacrifice fused into a single act of will.

chapters.title: Silence Like Snowfall
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The covenant reforges; the Hollow recedes like a tide going out. For the first time since childhood, Zephyrine hears nothing — no dead, no whispers, only Corvane breathing beside her. She grieves the loss and feels free. Emotional beat: bittersweet release; the cost honored, not regretted.

chapters.title: Accounts Settled
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. The guild is dissolved into a public trust; Odile faces the ghost-court she once dismissed, judged by the very dead she trafficked in. Sable Fen and the enforcers swear a new, transparent oath. Corvane declines command, giving the ledgers to the city. Emotional beat: justice rendered without vengeance; institutions rebuilt on consent.

chapters.title: The Carver Who Hears Nothing
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Epilogue. Zephyrine carves bones now purely as art, keeping a small shop above the river. A child brings her a relic that might whisper — and Zephyrine smiles, unable to hear it, and teaches the child to listen instead. Emotional beat: peace earned; the gift passed on, the hollow filled.
